sections.heading: Your right to a healthy environment
sections.body:
Every environment law builds on the [1987 Constitution](https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html).

- **Article II, Section 16:** "The State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature." (Section 15, just before it, is the right to *health*.)
- **Article XII, Section 2:** "wildlife, flora and fauna, and other natural resources are owned by the State."
- Only **agricultural lands** are **alienable**, or able to be sold to private owners (Sections 2 and 3).
- **Section 4:** national parks "may not be increased nor diminished, except by law."

**Method: find the provision, then match its key words.** "Who owns the wildlife?" Section 2 says "owned by the State."

sections.heading: Solid waste: RA 9003
sections.body:
Under [RA 9003](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2001/ra_9003_2001.html), the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, LGUs are "primarily responsible" (Section 10).

- **Segregation at source** (Section 21): sort waste where it is made. Containers are marked "compostable," "non-recyclable," "recyclable" or "special waste" (Section 22). Special waste is household hazardous waste, like paints and batteries.
- **Who collects** (Section 10): the barangay collects biodegradable, compostable and reusable waste; the municipality or city collects non-recyclables and special waste.
- **MRF** (Section 32): a Materials Recovery Facility "in every barangay or cluster of barangays."
- **Prohibited** (Section 48): littering in public places, "The open burning of solid waste," collecting unsorted waste, open dumps.
- **EPR** ([RA 11898](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2022/ra_11898_2022.html)): large enterprises that generate plastic packaging waste must recover it. Smaller enterprises are not covered.

**Method: check the act against the list of prohibited acts.** Burning garbage in the yard is open burning, so it is prohibited.

sections.heading: Clean air and clean water
sections.body:
The **DENR** leads both [RA 8749](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1999/ra_8749_1999.html), the Clean Air Act (Section 34), and [RA 9275](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2004/ra_9275_2004.html), the Clean Water Act (Section 19).

- RA 8749 recognizes "The right to breathe clean air" (Section 4) and that "polluters must pay" (Section 2).
- **Incineration ban** (RA 8749, Section 20): no burning of municipal, biomedical and hazardous waste. Crematoria are excluded.
- **Discharge permit** (RA 9275, Section 14): needed from the DENR before letting out **effluent**.
- **Clean-up** (RA 9275, Section 16): the polluter pays "at his own expense."
- **Prohibited** (RA 9275, Section 27(a)): putting material into water, or on its banks where floods could wash it in.

**Method: name who is responsible, then check the exact role.** "Who pays for an oil spill clean-up?" The polluter.

sections.heading: Protected areas and wildlife
sections.body:
The **E-NIPAS Act** ([RA 11038](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11038_2018.html), amending RA 7586) sets aside **protected areas** for their "unique physical and biological diversity." Each has a Protected Area Management Board (PAMB), chaired by the DENR Regional Director.

- **Buffer zone** (Section 4(c)): an area just outside a protected area that needs special development control.
- **Prohibited** (Section 20): kaingin (slash-and-burn farming), mineral exploration, exotic species, and permanent structures within 40 meters of the high water mark.
- **Wildlife** ([RA 9147](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2001/ra_9147_2001.html), Section 4): the DENR covers land species, wetland species and the dugong; the DA covers marine mammals "except dugong."
- Killing wildlife is illegal except in five cases, such as preventing imminent danger to human life (Section 27(a)).

**Method: match the term to its legal definition.** "Slash-and-burn cultivation" defines kaingin.

sections.heading: Climate change and disasters
sections.body:
[RA 9729](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2009/ra_9729_2009.html), the Climate Change Act (amended by [RA 10174](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10174_2012.html)), created the Climate Change Commission, chaired by the **President**. LGUs are "the frontline agencies" for local climate plans (Section 14). **Mitigation** cuts greenhouse gas emissions; **adaptation** adjusts to climate effects.

Under [RA 10121](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2010/ra_10121_2010.html), the DRRM Act of 2010:

- The **Secretary of National Defense** chairs the NDRRMC. The DILG, DSWD and DOST Secretaries are Vice Chairpersons for preparedness, response, and prevention and mitigation.
- LGUs set aside at least **5%** of estimated regular revenue as the LDRRMF; **30%** of it is the Quick Response Fund (Section 21).
- Selling, diverting or repacking relief goods to fake their source is prohibited (Section 19).
- Emergency response and preparedness training is **mandatory** for public sector employees (Section 14).

sections.heading: Common traps
sections.body:
- **Section 15 vs 16.** Health is Section 15; the environment is Section 16.
- **"Never" choices.** Parks can change "by law." Look for the exception.
- **Barangay vs city.** The municipality or city collects non-recyclables and special waste.
- **Sorting order.** Segregation starts at the source, not the MRF.
- **Dugong.** A marine mammal, but under the DENR, not the DA.
- **Two chairs.** The President chairs the Climate Change Commission; the Defense Secretary chairs the NDRRMC.

glossaryTerms.definition: Ecology is the relationship between living things and their surroundings. The Constitution protects the right to a balanced and healthful ecology.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Ecology – ugnayan ng mga buhay na nilalang at ng kanilang kapaligiran

glossaryTerms.definition: Land that is alienable can be sold or transferred to private owners. Among lands of the public domain, only agricultural lands are alienable.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Alienable – puwedeng ibenta o ilipat sa pribadong may-ari; sa public lands, agricultural lands lang

glossaryTerms.definition: Segregation at source means sorting waste into kinds at the place where it is produced, such as a home or office.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Segregation at source – paghihiwalay ng basura mismo sa bahay o opisina kung saan ito galing

glossaryTerms.definition: An MRF is a facility in a barangay or group of barangays that receives waste for final sorting, composting and recycling.
glossaryTerms.taglish: MRF – pasilidad sa barangay kung saan inaayos, kino-compost at nire-recycle ang basura

glossaryTerms.definition: Effluent is wastewater or other discharge from a known source, such as a factory, that flows into water or onto land.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Effluent – maruming tubig o discharge na lumalabas mula sa pabrika o establisimyento

glossaryTerms.definition: A buffer zone is an area just outside a protected area that needs special development control to protect it.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Buffer zone – lugar sa labas mismo ng protected area na may dagdag na proteksyon

glossaryTerms.definition: In climate change, mitigation is human action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and increase their removal.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Mitigation – pagbabawas ng greenhouse gas emissions para mabawasan ang sanhi ng climate change

glossaryTerms.definition: Adaptation is adjusting natural or human systems in response to the actual or expected effects of climate change.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Adaptation – pag-aangkop o pag-adjust sa epekto ng climate change
